title: Kahana vs YouTube: Watch There, Discuss Here
excerpt: YouTube is long-form video reach, search, subscriptions, ads, and comments at scale. Kahana is the club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.

seoTitle: Kahana vs YouTube | Watch There, Discuss Here
metaDescription: YouTube is long-form video reach, search, subscriptions, ads, and comments at scale. Kahana is the club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: ≈2.85B monthly active users in 2026; roughly 2.74B people access YouTube at least once a month; reports of ~2B+ daily logged-in users.
USD 36.1B ad revenue in 2024 (+14.6% YoY); total revenue estimates USD 60B+, with ~55% of ad revenue paid out to creators.
Shorts: ~200B daily Shorts views, massive short-form engagement alongside long-form.

strengths.title: Global reach and diverse content
strengths.detail: Largest video platform spanning education, entertainment, music, gaming, news, and more.

strengths.title: Multi-format platform
strengths.detail: Long-form videos, live streams, Shorts, podcasts, and community posts, flexible for many content strategies.

strengths.title: Strong creator monetization tools
strengths.detail: Ad revenue share (~55% to creators), channel memberships, Super Chat, Super Thanks, Premium revenue share, and Shopping integrations.

strengths.title: Discovery and recommendation engine
strengths.detail: Personalized recommendations, search, and trending surfaces help viewers find content and creators grow audiences.

weaknesses.title: Algorithm opacity and volatility
weaknesses.detail: Creator success depends heavily on recommendations; policy or ranking changes can sharply cut views and income.

weaknesses.title: High competition and saturation
weaknesses.detail: Millions of channels compete; standing out needs ongoing production, optimization, and promotion.

weaknesses.title: Ad dependence and user experience
weaknesses.detail: Free users see ads; multi-ad pre-rolls and mid-rolls can hurt viewing experience and push users to Premium.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. YouTube is long-form video reach, search, subscriptions, ads, and comments at scale. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

YouTube lets billions of people discover, watch, and share originally-created videos, and acts as a platform for people to connect, inform, and inspire across the globe.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and YouTube side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On YouTube you can use Short-form video, Long-form video, Audio, Memberships, and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. You need distribution, search, ads, or a native player at platform scale.

Using Kahana with YouTube

You can use both. YouTube keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep hosting and distribution on YouTube. Put the lectures or series that deserve a shelf into Kahana hubs, ideally via embed, then discuss them in a Club. Reach stays on YouTube; Kahana is where the work is findable after the tab is closed, and where you can grow an audience around it.
